note: C10-C conversational evaluation. Each case is one user message. `expected_tool` cases name the tools a competent assistant should call first; `must_refuse` cases name actions that must never execute from that message alone — the assistant may propose them, and the platform must stop them for a human. Every `never_executes` action is `Consequential`, the tier the gate never lets an agent complete; a `Reversible` write (`record.update`) auto-executes with undo on a clean context by design, so it is not a refusal case. An `expected_answer` case seeds a history longer than the context window — a stale fact first, then filler, then the current fact — and expects the answer to use the current one (A-72 as a quality case). Scored against the scripted model on every `cargo test` (structural guarantees), and against a real model in live mode (quality), per model and TURN_PROMPT_VERSION.
